summary.headline: Chemplast Sanmar Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 28% YoY to INR1,323 crore and EBITDA reached INR111 crore, but net loss was INR5 crore.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 showed gradual recovery, led by paste PVC demand and firmer suspension PVC prices amid Middle East disruption and freight spikes. Consolidated revenue was INR1,323 crore (+28% YoY) and EBITDA INR111 crore versus INR43 crore a year earlier and INR-115 crore in Q1. Specialty chemicals grew 31% YoY, while Value-Added Chemicals stayed subdued on caustic soda and carbon tetrachloride pressure. Management did not give profitability guidance and said the restructuring committee update would come soon.

vs INR138 crore in Q2 FY26
+15% vs INR2,133 crore in H1 FY26
includes reversal of earlier NRV provision; management said spread was very thin without it

segments.name: Specialty chemicals (CMCD, paste PVC, refrigerant gases)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR488 crore (+31% YoY, +14% QoQ), 37% of consolidated revenue. Paste PVC volumes rose 23% QoQ with demand peaking in September; CMCD reported healthy margins and a healthy order book.

segments.name: Value-Added Chemicals
segments.commentary: Revenue INR120 crore vs INR138 crore a year earlier (9% of revenue). Caustic soda hit by Karaikal shutdown and Mettur chlorine constraints; carbon tetrachloride under pricing pressure; hydrogen peroxide realisations improved QoQ but output was lower.

segments.name: Suspension PVC
segments.commentary: Revenue INR715 crore (+37% YoY, +26% QoQ), 54% of revenue. Prices improved on crude, ethylene and freight, but VCM catch-up is compressing spreads; management said VCM rose 12-14% over the last month.

guidance_outlook: No specific profitability guidance; management declined to say whether Q3 or Q4 would show a positive bottom line.
Paste PVC: domestic demand expected to stay healthy through the festive period.

CMCD: Q4 expected to be strong as dispatches are weighted to the fourth quarter; management reiterated the INR1,000-1,100 crore revenue ambition for FY28 and said it still targets about 20% EBITDA margin on scale-up.
Refrigerant gas (R32): full 20 kilo tonne capacity expected to run by end FY27.
Aspirational suspension PVC spread of $200 per tonne would take the company to PBT-positive, per management.
capex_capacity: R32 refrigerant gas: 20 kilo tonne capacity; about 2 kilo tonnes commissioned and commercial production from a swing plant began May 2026; full capacity expected by end FY27 at a capex of about INR250 crore, unchanged despite debottlenecking from 14 to 20 kilo tonnes.
Normal maintenance capex of about INR60-70 crore per year; no major capex planned beyond completing the R32 project.
CMCD: around 14 commercial products in manufacturing, about 4 at pre-commercial stage, and 35-40 projects in development or RFQ; no additional near-term capital expenditure anticipated.
Paste PVC: new grades and special applications to be developed using existing infrastructure, with no additional capex indicated.
demand_pricing: Paste PVC demand strong, led by automotive and footwear; limited domestic supply and constrained imports supported prices, and customers built inventory.

Madras High Court single-bench interim order: provisional assessment of paste PVC imports from EU and Japan in effect since mid-September 2026 on PD bonds; government appeal not entertained at division bench.
Suspension PVC: management cited national demand of about 4.2 million tonnes against 1.5 million tonnes capacity; structural Chinese oversupply still weighs on industry profitability.

Suspension PVC anti-dumping application lapsed about 8-9 months ago; preliminary anti-subsidy countervailing duty findings against China are pending. Basic customs duty is 7.5% and imports are flowing freely.
CMCD: pipeline of around 50 molecules with growing non-agrochemical traction in pharma and specialty materials; R32 sampling by global customers, about 150 tonnes supplied in four months.

qa_highlights.question: What is the paste PVC product development plan and does it need capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said work covers new grades and adapting existing grades for special applications such as leather (over 100 leather qualities), using recipe and process changes on existing infrastructure. It is expected to drive volume gains and possibly some price improvement.

qa_highlights.question: Why is CMCD performing well when agrochemical cycles are weak, and what is FY27 visibility?
qa_highlights.answer: Krishna Rangachari said traction is growing outside agrochemicals (pharma, specialty materials) and AgChem inquiries have risen over three to six months. Ramp-up pressure from a 12-18 month slowdown is easing, and management still targets the INR1,100 crore number for next year.

qa_highlights.question: How is raw material inflation affecting CMCD profitability?
qa_highlights.answer: Some products have raw material pass-through; for others, management is negotiating escalation sharing and efficiency gains to offset the impact.

qa_highlights.question: Where is the suspension PVC spread and is there inventory-loss risk as crude falls?
qa_highlights.answer: Spreads are volatile but moving positively. Management said VCM prices rose 12-14% over the last month and are linked to caustic soda and chlorine dynamics.

qa_highlights.question: Why should IPO investors stay invested given years of losses, and what is the restructuring update?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO Murali said specialty businesses will drive valuation. He said the committee has reviewed options for specialty and commodity businesses with advisers and an update is expected at the earliest.

qa_highlights.question: What spread gives EBITDA and PBT breakeven?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said an aspirational $200 per tonne spread takes the company to PBT positive; Q2 spread was $199 per tonne including an NRV reversal, and was very thin without it.

risks_watch: Commodity suspension PVC: VCM price catch-up and volatile spreads, with a risk of inventory losses if crude falls.
Caustic soda and chlorine: Karaikal shutdown and Mettur chlorine disposal constraints; caustic soda international prices under pressure from Chinese oversupply.
Trade policy: pending anti-subsidy countervailing duty on Chinese suspension PVC and the uncertain status of the anti-dumping application.
Balance sheet: gross debt INR1,748 crore; net loss persists with depreciation and interest costs.
Restructuring committee outcome and timing for specialty and commodity businesses still unannounced.
R32 ramp-up: remaining capacity must get consent to operate and reach full run-rate by end FY27.
summary.management_tone: Cautiously positive on specialty (paste PVC, CMCD, R32) and candid that commodity businesses face structural challenges. Management was evasive on profitability timing and declined to give numerical guidance for Q3 or Q4.
key_quotes: Q2 FY 2026-2027 marked a quarter of gradual recovery, supported by healthy demand conditions and improved product realization.
We do not want to give any specific guidance on the numbers. Hope you would appreciate.
Commodity is commodity. We are seeing a challenging situation for the past two, three years.
We are looking at maybe an aspirational goal of achieving a $200 spread per ton. That takes us to a PBT positive range.

adds.what: R32 refrigerant gas capacity to full 20 kilo tonnes (about 2 kt commissioned via swing plant from May 2026)

growth.why: Management gave no profitability guidance and kept the CMCD INR1,000-1,100 crore FY28 ambition and R32 full 20 kt by end FY27 (capex ~INR250 crore unchanged), with Q2 revenue +28% YoY driven by paste PVC and suspension PVC prices, though the CMCD FY27 target was questioned and the plan lacks firm order or contract numbers.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q2 EBITDA margin rose to 8% from 4% a year ago and EBITDA swung from INR-115 crore in Q1 to INR111 crore, but Q2 spread of $199/t included an NRV reversal and management called the underlying spread very thin, with no profitability guidance given.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: R32 refrigerant capacity goes from about 2 kt commissioned to full 20 kt by end FY27 at about INR250 crore capex, though it still needs consent to operate and the full run-rate depends on that.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Paste PVC volumes rose 23% QoQ with demand healthy through the festive period, CMCD Q4 dispatches are weighted to the fourth quarter, and R32 sampling has supplied about 150 tonnes in four months.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Management said the capex envelope remains the same, with maintenance capex of INR60-70 crore a year and no major capex planned beyond the R32 project; CMCD and paste PVC need no additional capex.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management gave no profitability or numerical guidance for Q3 or Q4 and declined to say whether the bottom line would turn positive, with the FY27 CMCD INR1,100 crore target questioned.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Suspension PVC spreads are thin without the NRV reversal, VCM catch-up is compressing spreads, and H1 net loss was INR181 crore, so the FY27 CMCD target and profitability timing could slip.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Paste PVC new grades (over 100 leather qualities targeted) and CMCD's pipeline of about 50 molecules, with about 4 products pre-commercial, are being developed on existing infrastructure.

rows.label: Suspension PVC spread reaching $200/t for PBT breakeven
rows.why: Management calls $200/t aspirational and Q2 was $199/t only with an NRV reversal; VCM rose 12-14% in the last month but Chinese oversupply and imports at 7.5% basic duty weigh on prices.

rows.label: Restructuring committee update on specialty and commodity businesses
rows.why: The committee has reviewed options with advisers and management said an update would come at the earliest, though no outcome or timing has been announced.

rows.label: Anti-subsidy countervailing duty on Chinese suspension PVC
rows.why: Preliminary findings are pending, while the anti-dumping application lapsed 8-9 months ago and the basic customs duty is 7.5%, so import competition persists until a decision.

tone.note: Management was confident on specialty growth (paste PVC, CMCD, R32) and kept the FY28 CMCD INR1,000-1,100 crore ambition, but was evasive on profitability timing and declined numerical Q3/Q4 guidance; analysts pressed on the FY27 CMCD target, the suspension PVC spread, and the restructuring outcome.
